subject: Customer-friendly data movement explainer for Hosted API & Console
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — plain-language data movement explainer for DPA/console

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. Our procurement and security teams are asking for a short (1-2 paragraph) explainer that we can surface in the Acme developer portal and link from our legal signoff docs. They want something customer-facing that explains, at a high level: where data goes when we call Redwood's hosted API and what subprocessors (if any) are involved for transit, storage, and logging.

Two constraints from Legal:
- Keep the language non-technical and suitable for product documentation.
- Call out any cross-border transfers and the default safeguards.

I've attached a PDF with their template and some callouts. Can your team provide a brief draft plus a simple diagram we can paste into our internal packet? Ideally by EOD July 2 so we can make the RFP deadline.

Appreciate it —
Sofia

Attachments: acme_request_initial.pdf (PDF: procurement template and Qs)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — plain-language data movement explainer for DPA/console

Hi Sofia —

Thanks — we can do that. Attaching an early draft of a 2-paragraph explainer and a simple data-flow PNG for your packet. The draft keeps technical details minimal and calls out subprocessors and cross-border transfer safeguards.

Kimberly, Vivek, Marissa — looping you in for legal & product signoff. Specific asks:
- Kimberly: quick privacy/legal review for accuracy and any redlines (esp. subprocessors wording).
- Vivek: confirm the phrasing around temporary inference caching (we've avoided deep infra terms but want the wording to be safe).
- Marissa: confirm this aligns with console copy size/format (we may publish a shortened variant in the Console help panel).

Sofia, ETA: we expect a redlined version back by Thu July 1, final by EOD July 2 if that works.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: data_flow_diagram_v1.png (PNG: simple boxes showing client -> hosted API -> GPU pool -> optional storage), dpa_plainlanguage_v1.docx (DOCX: 2-paragraph explainer)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — plain-language data movement explainer for DPA/console

Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft. Quick redlines and comments below (copied into the attached doc for ease):

1) Subprocessors: please list "cloud provider for compute" and "logging provider" rather than vendor names in the public snippet; Acme's procurement can request the full subprocessor list under the DPA.
2) Caching language: replace any infrastructure-specific term like "KV cache" with "temporary inference cache" — that wording reduces technical leakage while being accurate.
3) Cross-border transfers: add one sentence about safeguards — e.g., standard contractual clauses and region-specific hosting options — and confirm that customers can choose region-restricted deployments via Dedicated/Private.
4) Data retention: clarify that by default we do not persist user request payloads beyond short-term logs used for reliability/abuse detection unless a customer opts into extended retention for debugging or analytics.

Suggested public paragraph (for console help panel):
"When you send a request to Redwood's hosted API, the request is routed to our secure serving environment in the region you select. We process the request and return a response in real time. For short-term performance, we may use a temporary inference cache; we do not use requests to train models. We work with a small set of subprocessors to enable compute and core platform logging — customers can request the full subprocessor list under the DPA. Cross-border transfers are handled under contractual safeguards, and customers can choose region-restricted deployments for stricter data residency requirements."

I've attached a marked-up doc (dpa_plainlanguage_v1_kp.docx) and a short redline of the PNG legend. If you want, I can produce a 1-paragraph variant for the public Console help panel that fits within 300 characters.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_plainlanguage_v1_kp.docx (DOCX: redlines and suggested language)

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — plain-language data movement explainer for DPA/console

Hi Laura / Kimberly —

This is great — thanks to the team for the rapid response and for keeping the wording customer-friendly. The procurement team liked the suggested paragraph and the diagram with the updated legend. A couple quick questions before we finalize:

- Can you confirm in one line that hosted API requests are never used to train public models (we saw the "we do not use requests to train models" sentence but would like explicit confirmation that this is the default behavior for hosted API)?
- Is there a short, 250–300 character version we can paste into the portal as a tooltip?

If you can send the final copy and the short tooltip piece by EOD today (July 2) we'll include it in our packet.

Thanks again —
Sofia Ramirez
Security & Procurement Lead
Acme Health
